org.apache.lucene.analysis.AbstractAnaly.reason: getPattern returns a java.util.regex.Pattern. The crate has no regular-expression engine of that kind (util::automaton::RegExp implements Lucene's own regexp syntax over an automaton, not Java's), so porting it means adopting a new dependency. CLAUDE.md 13.3 requires the user's approval before adopting a dependency, so this one member is held open pending that decision rather than resolved unilaterally.
org.apache.lucene.analysis.AbstractAnaly.triageReason: Deferred, not inapplicable: getPattern needs a regular-expression dependency the user has not approved. The contract still has no Rust item discharging it.

org.apache.lucene.analysis.standard.Stan.reason: Lucene's scanner is generated by JFlex from StandardTokenizerImpl.jflex; these members are the generated packed tables and the JFlex reader protocol that drives them. This port applies the same UAX #29 rules through the unicode-segmentation crate instead of transcribing a generated automaton. Declared on the type in src/analysis/standard.rs and in specs/modules/standard-tokenizer-strategy.md.
org.apache.lucene.analysis.standard.Stan.triageReason: These are the packed tables and reader protocol of a JFlex-generated scanner: they exist only because of Java's code generator, which this port replaces with the same UAX #29 rules through unicode-segmentation.

org.apache.lucene.document.LatLonPoint.reason: newDistanceFeatureQuery returns a LatLonPointDistanceFeatureQuery, which scores by distance rather than matching at a constant score, so it needs its own Weight and Scorer rather than the spatial constant-score path; nearest() needs the NearestNeighbor search over several readers to be exposed as a public entry point. Both are tracked as their own gaps.
org.apache.lucene.document.LatLonPoint.triageReason: Deferred, not inapplicable: blocked on the geo query types implementing the Query trait. The contract still has no Rust item discharging it.

org.apache.lucene.internal.vectorization.reason: Stable Rust has no portable SIMD (std::simd is nightly-only), so the jdk.incubator.vector lane kernels cannot be reproduced. PanamaVectorConstants::PREFERRED_VECTOR_BITSIZE is zero, every lane guard fails, and the whole computation runs Lucene's own scalar tail through DefaultVectorUtilSupport. The divergence is declared in src/internal/vectorization/panama_vector_util_support.rs.
org.apache.lucene.internal.vectorization.triageReason: These are jdk.incubator.vector lane kernels: they exist only because of a Java construct (the Panama Vector API) that this port does not have, so there is no contract for a Rust item to discharge.

org.apache.lucene.search.PointRangeQuery.reason: checkArgs(String, Object, Object) rejects a null field, a null lowerPoint and a null upperPoint (PointRangeQuery.java:106). Rust has no null: the port takes &str and Vec<u8>, so all three checks are discharged by the type system at every call site the Java helper guards. The divergence is declared on PointRangeQuery::new in src/search/point_range_query.rs, which keeps the three checks that remain expressible.
org.apache.lucene.search.PointRangeQuery.triageReason: The method exists only to reject null, a value the port's types cannot hold. There is no contract left for a Rust item to discharge.

org.apache.lucene.util.BytesRefBuilder.reason: Lucene's BytesRefBuilder.equals(Object) and BytesRefBuilder.hashCode() both `throw new UnsupportedOperationException()` (BytesRefBuilder.java:166 and :171): a mutable builder must never be used as a map key nor compared by value, and Lucene enforces that at runtime. The faithful port of a method whose whole body is a throw is to leave the trait unimplemented, so the port implements neither PartialEq nor Hash for BytesRefBuilder and Java's runtime failure becomes a compile error. The divergence is declared on the type in src/util.rs.
org.apache.lucene.util.BytesRefBuilder.triageReason: There is no contract to discharge: the Java method exists only to forbid the call, which Rust forbids at compile time by the absence of the trait. A Rust item answering it would have to reintroduce the failure Lucene raises.

The faithful port of a method whose whole body is a throw is to leave the trait unimplemented, so the port implements neither PartialEq nor Hash for CharsRefBuilder and Java's runtime failure becomes a compile error. The divergence is declared on the type in src/util/refs.rs.

The faithful port of a method whose whole body is a throw is to leave the trait unimplemented, so the port implements neither PartialEq nor Hash for IntsRefBuilder and Java's runtime failure becomes a compile error. The divergence is declared on the type in src/util/refs.rs.

org.apache.lucene.index.CheckIndex.reason: main(String[]) is `System.exit(doMain(args))`. A library crate has no process to exit and no `main`; `doMain` is ported as the public `check_index::do_main`, which returns the exit code Java hands to `System.exit`, and the divergence is declared on that item. This is the same shape `LockVerifyServer::main` and `LockStressTest::main` already take.
org.apache.lucene.index.CheckIndex.triageReason: The method exists only to turn doMain's return value into a process exit code, which a library crate has nothing to do with; doMain itself is ported and returns that code.

org.apache.lucene.index.CorruptIndexExce.reason: The port's CorruptIndex error variant carries the composed message rather than Java's separate `message` and `resourceDescription` fields, because 232 call sites construct it directly with an already-composed string. The divergence, and why the two parts cannot be recovered from the composed one, is declared on `LuceneError::corrupt_index` in src/error.rs.
org.apache.lucene.index.CorruptIndexExce.triageReason: The field it reads does not exist: the port keeps one composed message, a divergence declared at the constructor. The rendered message is identical to Java's.

org.apache.lucene.index.DocumentsWriterP.reason: `DocumentsWriterPerThread implements java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock`. `isHeldByCurrentThread()` exists only to be asserted, and the port's `DwptGuard` proves the same thing in the type system — every operation Java guards with `assert isHeldByCurrentThread()` is a method on the guard. `lockInterruptibly()` rests on JVM thread interruption, which Rust has no equivalent of, and Lucene never calls it on a DWPT. `newCondition()` throws UnsupportedOperationException in Lucene. All three are declared on `DocumentsWriterPerThread::lock`.
org.apache.lucene.index.DocumentsWriterP.triageReason: Members of the `Lock` interface the class implements: one is an assertion the RAII guard makes structural, one needs JVM thread interruption, and one throws UnsupportedOperationException in Lucene itself.

org.apache.lucene.index.FrozenBufferedUp.reason: `unlock()` releases the `applyLock` a matching `lock()`/`tryLock()` took. The port returns a `MutexGuard` from `lock_apply`/`try_lock_apply`, so the release is the guard's `Drop` — there is no separate method to call, and no way to call it twice or forget it.
org.apache.lucene.index.FrozenBufferedUp.triageReason: An explicit unlock has no counterpart where the lock hands back an RAII guard; releasing is dropping the guard.

org.apache.lucene.index.FieldUpdatesBuff.reason: Java packs the updates into parallel primitive arrays plus a BytesRefArray and elides a repeated field name or value; this port keeps one record per update, a divergence declared on the type. `getArrayIndex(int,int)` resolves an ordinal into a possibly-elided array, `sizeOfString(String)` accounts the elided String[], and `assertTermAndDocInOrder()` validates the sort state `finish()` builds for the sorted-terms optimisation this port never takes. All three exist only to serve the packed representation.
org.apache.lucene.index.FieldUpdatesBuff.triageReason: Artefacts of the packed parallel-array representation the port replaces with one record per update, declared on the type; the iteration order, docUpTo semantics and numeric/binary split are unchanged.

org.apache.lucene.index.TermsHash.reason: The bodies of `startDocument()`, `finishDocument(int)` and `flush(Map, SegmentWriteState, Sorter.DocMap, NormsProducer)` on the abstract TermsHash are, in their entirety, `if (nextTermsHash != null) nextTermsHash.<same>()`: they walk the chain Lucene builds from the freq-prox hash to the term-vectors hash. This port gives the term-vectors consumer its own TermsHash and has no `nextTermsHash` link — declared in the `freq_prox_terms_writer` module notes and again on `TermsHash::abort` — so the indexing chain calls both consumers directly, in Lucene's order.
org.apache.lucene.index.TermsHash.triageReason: Chain-walking methods whose whole body is a forward to `nextTermsHash`; the port has no chain, and the concrete overrides that do real work are ported on the consumers.

org.apache.lucene.index.TermsHashPerFiel.reason: `start(IndexableField, boolean)` and `finish()` on the abstract base forward to `nextPerField`, and `getNextPerField()` returns that link — the chain this port does not build. `newPostingsArray()` re-takes a downcast of the abstract `ParallelPostingsArray` into the subclass's typed view, and `createPostingsArray(int)` is the factory the subclass supplies; the port stores one concrete `FreqProxPosting` struct per term in a `Vec`, so there is no abstract array to downcast and no factory to call. Both are declared in the `freq_prox_terms_writer` module notes.
org.apache.lucene.index.TermsHashPerFiel.triageReason: The chain link and the postings-array factory of a class hierarchy the port replaces with one concrete type and an array of structs.

org.apache.lucene.index.FreqProxTermsWri.reason: `start(IndexableField, boolean)` calls `super.start` and then caches the three `TokenStream` attribute objects (`termFreqAtt`, `payloadAttribute`, `offsetAttribute`) off `fieldState`; this port passes the values in each `InvertedToken`, so there is nothing to cache. `newPostingsArray()` and `createPostingsArray(int)` are the downcast and the factory of the `ParallelPostingsArray` hierarchy the port replaces with one struct per term. All three are declared in the `freq_prox_terms_writer` module notes.
org.apache.lucene.index.FreqProxTermsWri.triageReason: Attribute caching the port has no attributes for, plus the postings-array factory hooks of a hierarchy replaced by one concrete type.

org.apache.lucene.index.TermVectorsConsu.reason: `createPostingsArray(int)` builds the `TermVectorsPostingsArray` that `TermsHashPerField` holds as the abstract `ParallelPostingsArray`. The columns of that subclass are fields of the single `FreqProxPosting` struct this port stores per term, so there is no separate array to construct; the sibling `newPostingsArray()` is ported precisely to declare that there is nothing left to re-take.
org.apache.lucene.index.TermVectorsConsu.triageReason: The postings-array factory of a hierarchy the port replaces with one struct per term.

org.apache.lucene.index.ParallelPostings.reason: `newInstance(int)` is the abstract factory each subclass overrides, and `copyTo(ParallelPostingsArray, int)` copies the parallel columns into a grown instance of the same subclass. This port stores one `FreqProxPosting` struct per term in a `Vec`, so growth is `Vec`'s own and there is neither a subclass to instantiate nor parallel columns to copy across. Declared in the `freq_prox_terms_writer` module notes.
org.apache.lucene.index.ParallelPostings.triageReason: The grow-and-copy protocol of a parallel-array hierarchy the port replaces with a Vec of structs.
